learning_objective: 🎯 Become a financial detective! Learn to read boring balance sheets and convert them into percentages to easily see if a company is growing or failing.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: This compares a company's performance over two different years (Year 1 vs. Year 2). You find the absolute change in rupees, and then convert that change into a percentage to spot growth or decline.

This takes one single year and sets a 'Base' to 100%. For the Balance Sheet, Total Assets = 100%. Then you calculate what percentage of the total is made of Cash, Machinery, etc. It helps compare a tiny company to a giant company!
Looking at data over 3, 4, or 5 years to see the direction the business is moving. Is sales going steadily up, or fluctuating wildly?

Financial analysis isn't perfect. It ignores inflation (price changes), ignores qualitative factors (like a hardworking team), and is based on historical (past) data which might not predict the future.

fun_activity.title: 📊 The Exam Score Trend
fun_activity.instructions: Take your total marks from 10th grade and 11th grade. Calculate the Absolute Change (11th marks - 10th marks). Now find the Percentage Change: (Absolute Change / 10th marks) * 100. You just did a Comparative Analysis of yourself!

exam_tips: 📌 Formula for Comparative Percentage Change: $(Current Year - Previous Year) / Previous Year \times 100$. NEVER divide by the current year!
📌 In a Common-Size Statement of Profit & Loss, the Base (100%) is ALWAYS 'Revenue from Operations' (Net Sales). Every expense is calculated as a percentage of Sales.
📌 When writing limitations of analysis, always mention 'Window Dressing'—the practice where companies manipulate accounts to look better than they really are.
quick_recap: ⭐ Comparative statements compare multiple years (Horizontal analysis).
⭐ Common-size statements analyze a single year by converting all figures to percentages of a base (Vertical analysis).
⭐ Financial analysis only shows the numbers; it cannot measure the quality of management or inflation.
